result.stdout:
SageFs - F# Interactive daemon with MCP, hot reloading, and live dashboard

Usage: SageFs [options]                Start daemon (default mode)
       SageFs check                    Check environment before first run
       SageFs install-skill [--force]  Install the sagefs agent skill (~/.claude/skills; --dir <folder>)
       SageFs setup [--client C] [--dir D] [--write]
                                       Register SageFs as a stdio server in Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop (C is claude-code, vscode,
                                       cursor or claude-desktop). Prints what it would do; --write merges the entry into the client's config and installs the skill
       SageFs member mint --role R (--dir D | --session ID) [--scope S] [--ttl MINUTES] [--print-env VAR]
                                       Mint a member token with the operator credential (operator.token); --print-env prints an export line
       SageFs cohort seat [<member id> [--replace <holder id>]] [--dir D]
                                       Fill an empty conductor seat with a present member (operator.token); with --replace, take the seat from a holder whose connection is gone;
                                       with no member id, list who is present and where the seat stands (and whether the holder is silent)
       SageFs data clear [--store friction|cohort|all]
                                       Clear the local stores SageFs keeps (operator.token); a running cohort's ledger is left alone
       SageFs call --list              List the daemon's tools (name and first line of the description)
       SageFs call <tool> [--<parameter> <value> ...] | --json '{...}'
                                       Call one tool and print its answer. Values are typed from the tool's own input schema;
                                       a tool error goes to stderr with exit code 1. --token T or SAGEFS_MEMBER_TOKEN is the member
                                       it calls as (none is anonymous); --port P 
[truncated]

result.stdout:
usage: sagefs call --list
       sagefs call <tool> [--<parameter> <value> ...]
       sagefs call <tool> --json '{"parameter": value}'
       sagefs call <tool> --help

  --list           list the daemon's tools: name and first line of the description
  --help           with a tool's name, print what that tool does and takes (needs the daemon); alone, this text
  --json <object>  the tool's arguments as one JSON object (instead of --<parameter> flags)
  --token-file <path>  read the member token to call as from a file ('-' reads standard input)
                   the default is SAGEFS_MEMBER_TOKEN, and with none the call is anonymous
  --token <token>  the same, but the token is typed on the command line, where the process list and the shell
                   history keep it. Deprecated: use SAGEFS_MEMBER_TOKEN or --token-file
  --port <port>    the daemon's MCP port (default: --mcp-port, SAGEFS_MCP_PORT, then 37749)

A flag takes its value from the next word or after '=' (--code=--help for a value that starts with '--').
A value is typed from the tool's own input schema. A boolean flag alone means true.
Output is the tool's answer on stdout. A tool that answers with an error goes to stderr, exit code 1.
